claim_label: Liability-based deterrence versus participatory governance requirements
description: This conflict debates whether uncapped strict liability effectively prevents discriminatory deployment or if mandatory participatory vetoes are essential to ensure accountability.

instances.assertion: Uncapped strict liability is sufficient to deter discriminatory deployment; participatory vetoes act as unnecessary friction that creates regulatory moats.
Liability will inevitably be capped or insured away by political and judicial processes; participatory governance is the only non-negotiable decision gate that prevents deployment.
